reason: E3 directly supports that Si forms silicides enabling precipitation hardening in RHEAs, and E1 shows RHEA strength drops significantly near 1223 K, consistent with the baseline softening. However, no cited evidence addresses the specific TiVNbTa alloy, the proposed 0.25 Si fraction, or the mechanism of dislocation pinning by silicides in this system; E2 only provides general RHEA background, and E4 contradicts the premise by showing high strength retention without Si.
premises: Si addition to RHEAs can form silicide precipitates that provide precipitation strengthening
Precipitation hardening via silicides can address BCC-phase strengthening limitations in RHEAs
RHEAs retain strength at high temperatures, with softening occurring above ~1223 K
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy loses strength at 1273 K due to thermally activated dislocation glide
Fine precipitates can pin dislocations and reduce high-temperature softening
